I've written `index.html` in your project folder: one file with all the CSS inline and no build step. The only things it loads from outside are Google Fonts, and it falls back to system fonts if those don't load. I couldn't open it in a browser here because the commands to check for one needed your approval, so I haven't seen how it looks or tested it on a phone.

**The page, top to bottom:**
- **Hero:** your README's headline and tagline, the install command with a copy button, a link to Getting started, and three short facts: Node 22 or newer, no key needed for the first run, and every run is kept.
- **The banking77 run:** the six-model table from the README shown as bars, plus a strip showing that the models agreed on 70 cases and differed on 10. Under it is the README's line that this is not a ranking, with a link to the example.
- **How it works:** three steps, each with a sample command: write a rubric, ask every model, read where they disagree.
- **Try it:** the commands for the first run (no API key) and for your own cases in a terminal-style block, next to the environment variable each service needs.
- **Models and inputs:** your models table with a "live-checked" column, and the six input types shown as cards.
- **After you've chosen a model:** cards for Version it, Use it from any machine, Bring in people, Call it from code, and Judge more than text, each linking to its docs page.
- **Packages:** each npm command with its own copy button.
- **Closing call to action and footer:** links to the docs, issues, changelog, contributing and security pages, plus the MIT and BANKING77 attribution.

The look is warm off-white with a serif headline, monospace for commands and one rust-red accent. There's a dark mode that follows the system setting and also has a toggle that remembers your choice. The layout narrows for phones, and sections fade in as you scroll unless the visitor has reduced motion turned on.

All the copy and numbers come from the README, and I made up no stars, logos or testimonials. The GitHub links assume your default branch is `main`, so check that.
